document.abstract: The International Telecommunication Union (ITU) is the specialized agency of the United Nations (UN) for information and communication technologies. Its primary roles are to allocate global radio-frequency spectrum and satellite orbits, develop the technical standards that ensure networks and technologies seamlessly interconnect, and strive to improve access to information communication technologies (ICTs) to underserved communities worldwide.

authors.bio: Yukihiro Nishida is an executive research engineer (Fellow) at the Science and Technology Research Laboratories, Japan Broadcasting Corporation (NHK), Tokyo, Japan. He is chair of ITU-R SG 6.
authors.name: Yukihiro Nishida

authors.bio: Amir Nafez is the general director of technical evaluation, supervision, and frequency planning at the Islamic Republic of Iran Broadcasting (IRIB), Teheran, Iran, the exclusive national broadcaster of Iran since 2014. Since joining IRIB in 1995, he has been responsible for TV and radio network planning. He is chair of ITU-R WP 6A.
authors.name: Amir Nafez

authors.bio: Paul Gardiner is the standards manager in the Advanced Technology Team of European Professional Engineering, Sony Europe B.V., Basingstoke, U.K. He is a chartered engineer, a member of the U.K.’s Institution of Engineering and Technology and a SMPTE Fellow. He is chair of ITU-R WP 6B.
authors.name: Paul Gardiner

authors.bio: Andy Quested joined the BBC as a technical assistant in 1978, becoming a videotape editor in 1985, where he worked on many comedy, children’s, and documentary series. He is chair of ITU-R WP 6C, co-chair of the ITU’s Accessible Media group, led the EBU Production Strategic programme and is a SMPTE Fellow.
authors.name: Andy Quested
